summary: A brick keeper's dwelling and tower of 1858 at the tip of the Leelanau Peninsula, replacing a first light of 1852; Coast Guard crews left in 1972 and a museum has run it since 1987.

access.note: Museum open seasonally April to December; tower climbable in season; inside Leelanau State Park, Recreation Passport required.

stay.note: Keeper program since 2004 lets visitors stay in the assistant keeper's quarters (Lighthouse Friends).

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree: first tower (brick, LF; rubble stone, museum), construction start (late 1851 vs spring 1852), dwelling conversion (1900 vs 1901), focal height (103 ft museum vs 40 ft USLHS), Dame second term (1923 vs 1928), keeper Marken/Marten, group founding (1984 vs 1985), reopening (1986 half vs 1987). Lighthouse Friends/museum text is copyrighted and paraphrased; Pepper's text is second-hand. Raids by Strang's followers are reported without dated sources, and LF says 'four years' for Moon, inconsistent with a one-year term. Whether the skeletal-tower light is still lit is unresolved in the record. 1896-97 volume cited without printed page. No newspapers read (loc.gov search timed out). Roster from USLHS only; Terry Pepper roster not cross-checked. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Bette McCormick Olli is called a child of 'John and Mary McCormick' by LF though the keeper is James; story states this rather than calling her his daughter. LF also says Moon served 'four years' and a fourth-order lens in 1857; both noted. Barn date 1880 (museum) vs 1891 (report/LF) stated. 1900 report page checked on page image (printed p.147, 183 hours, 18 cords). Coast Guard crew roster added from USLHS.
